# OneLobby

> Open-source, game-agnostic multiplayer kit: lobby server with join codes, TURN relay, WebRTC data-channel clients for
> JavaScript, .NET, Godot 4 C# and Unity 6. Lockstep or raw messaging, host-authoritative state replication (.NET), voice
> and text chat, self-hostable, games stay playable offline.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what OneLobby is, the API on one screen for C# and JS, and the rules
- [examples/tictactoe/README.md](examples/tictactoe/README.md): a single-player browser game to practise on

Lobby events (JS `lobby.on(name)`; C# has PascalCase events for most, e.g. `PeerReady`, `MessageReceived`): peerJoined, peerReady (data link to that peer open; reliable
sends made before it are queued and flushed, not dropped), ready and the `lobby.ready` promise (C# `Ready`, `ReadyAsync`:
a joiner's link to the host is open; the host is ready at once), peerLeft, joinRequested, hostChanged, phase,
message, metaChanged, serverLost, sessionEnded.

JS defaults: host() is unlisted unless visibility "public"; empty displayName shows as "Player N"; a joiner that cannot
reach the host in readyTimeoutMs (15000) fails with code ice_failed (sessionEnded reason "ice_failed"); rememberSeat keeps
the seat across a reload (kit.resume(), kit.rememberedCode); seams go under options.advanced; describeError(e),
shareUrl(code) and codeFromUrl() are player-facing helpers. C#: OneLobbyConfig.ReadyTimeout (15 s, Zero = forever)
does the same as readyTimeoutMs (ReadyAsync faults with OneLobbyException code ice_failed); Unity's OneLobbyRunner keeps
Application.runInBackground on while in a lobby (KeepRunningInBackground); ReplicationSession.Clients counts a peer only
once its link is up (ClientReady). Install: npm install onelobby, or the script-tag
build dist/onelobby.global.min.js (window.OneLobby).

## Recipes

- [Blueprint flow](.claude/skills/onelobby/SKILL.md): survey a game, write onelobby.json (schema [spec/blueprint.schema.json](spec/blueprint.schema.json), design [docs/design/blueprint.md](docs/design/blueprint.md)), build with OneLobby.fromConfig / Blueprint.Load, verify two players
- [Godot 4 C#](docs/recipes/godot-csharp.md): Host / Join / Browse buttons in a Godot project
- [Unity 6](docs/recipes/unity.md): the com.onelobby.unity package (UnityTransport over OneLobby.DataChannel/libdatachannel, OneLobbyRunner, voice); desktop now, no WebGL
- [Browser JS](docs/recipes/js-web.md): the same in a plain web page
- [Generic .NET](docs/recipes/dotnet-generic.md): console or any engine; DataChannelTransport (libdatachannel WebRTC) for real play, the in-memory transport for tests
- [Raw mode](docs/recipes/raw-mode.md): bring your own netcode (host-authoritative, turn-based)
- [Replicated state](docs/recipes/replication.md): OneLobby.Replication (C#) on raw mode: delta snapshots, interpolation, inputs, events, prediction, lag-compensated hitscan
- [Voice and chat](docs/recipes/voice-and-chat.md): push-to-talk, mute, text chat
- [Headless testing](docs/recipes/testing.md): two browser contexts with playwright-core, fake mic
- [Host with a join code](docs/recipes/direct-ip.md): no server at all; the host's .NET game or Node server runs the hub, opens port 47810 TCP+UDP on the router (UPnP/NAT-PMP) and shows a join code that is its address; joiners in C#, Node or a browser paste it
- [Browser game hosted from Node](docs/recipes/browser-game.md): the host's Node game server is a direct host that serves the game page on port 47810; friends open one link, the page joins the address it came from through a WebSocket-shaped adapter (heartbeat, rate limit, fallback when WebRTC is missing)
- [Self-host](docs/recipes/self-host.md): run the lobby server and relay yourself (hosted backend, later)

## API reference (generated by docs/build.mjs)

- [JS client](docs/api/js.md): every export of onelobby
- [.NET client](docs/api/dotnet.md): every public type of OneLobby.Core, OneLobby.Godot and OneLobby.Replication

- [Run your own server](deploy/RUN_YOUR_OWN.md): five steps, port table, smoke test
